briefs.headline: Reds answer with an 11-5 win in Arizona
briefs.summary: A night after being shut out, Cincinnati took 16 hits. Rhett Lowder got the win at 5-8 and Michael Soroka fell to 8-4.

briefs.headline: The Dodgers edge the Pirates 4-3, a second one-run loss
briefs.summary: Pittsburgh dropped its second straight by a run in Los Angeles. Yohan Ramirez took the loss and Tanner Scott closed for his 19th save.

briefs.headline: Buffalo routs the Browns 31-7 in Cleveland
briefs.summary: The Browns managed 194 yards and 3.7 a play in preseason week two before 69,035; Luke Floriea's touchdown catch was the lone score.

briefs.headline: Bengals put away the Bears 27-9 at Paycor
briefs.summary: Josh Johnson went 15 of 23 for 156 yards and two touchdowns; Evan McPherson was perfect on two field goals and three extra points.

briefs.headline: Brentford beat Tottenham 3-0 in the league opener
briefs.summary: Lewis-Potter, Janelt and Kayode all scored by the 49th minute; manager Roberto De Zerbi said his side 'were not ready to fight.'

briefs.headline: Nashville sink the Crew 3-2 in stoppage time
briefs.summary: Mohamed Farsi and Andre Gomes had Columbus ahead 2-1 until the 90th minute; Nashville scored at 90+2 and 90+4 to take it.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati held 1-1 by Seattle at TQL Stadium
briefs.summary: Evander scored in the 24th minute; Kossa-Rienzi equalized in the 83rd against 71% Cincinnati possession.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: Hull stun Manchester United 2-0 on their return
briefs.summary: Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy scored first-half set-piece goals in Hull's first top-flight match since 2017; Marcus Rashford returned after 618 days out and United never threatened.

briefs.headline: Milwaukee move to 81-49 behind Henderson
briefs.summary: The Brewers beat Atlanta 4-1 as Logan Henderson improved to 8-2 with a 2.60 ERA; the Cubs sit seven back in the NL Central.

briefs.headline: Sumo's Aki rankings sheet is eight days out
briefs.summary: The banzuke, the rankings, is due Aug. 31 and remains the next confirmed date on the calendar; the JSA's English pages still carry no September schedule, only that every day is sold out.

sections.note: Sumo got its own search again, and for the first morning since Aug. 19 the fan wire answered. It carried a significant injury report about a top-division wrestler, but no outlet this desk can open and cite carries it - the Japan Times sumo desk now returns a paywall - so it does not run. A Sept. 13-27 Aki opening at Ryogoku Kokugikan is still derived from the second-Sunday rule and remains uncited by the JSA, a tenth straight morning.

sections.note: Nothing closes in either state inside the next two weeks. West Virginia has no general season open until the youth squirrel weekend, which is why the WV calendar is short in August. Migratory bird dates - geese, ducks, doves, woodcock and snipe - are not in the pamphlet's summary table and come from a separate WVDNR publication issued in August; HIP registration is required.

waters.read: 242 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.
waters.working: Off 346 cfs a day ago, so the storm water keeps draining. It is still a heavy-nymph-on-the-seam river: a weighted stonefly or a sculpin along the undercut banks and the soft inside edges. One more day of this fall puts it near 200 cfs, which is wading water again.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.0 ft and falling - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: At pool and still easing, which holds fish on structure. Shad are the forage: a white swimbait across the wing dams and the riprap first, and the lock wall as the water keeps clearing.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 27.8 ft and falling - up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Down another two-thirds of a foot on the day and closing on the pool side, but still high and carrying colour. The slack behind rock and the wall stays the pattern, with a crawfish-coloured crankbait tight to the riprap; the bite improves as this keeps dropping.

waters.reading: Sound highs 4:55 AM at 3.0 ft and 5:40 PM at 3.9 ft at Hampstead; lows 11:12 AM at 0.5 ft and 12:07 AM (Mon) at 1.1 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 4:55 AM and 5:40 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Tide before lure. The fall off the dawn high runs to a low 11:12 a.m. low of half a foot, and that long late-morning ebb is the red drum window - the last of it along the grass edges and oyster bars with cut menhaden or finger mullet. The moon is a waxing gibbous at 77%, ten days old and building toward the full, so spring tides are stiffening the inlet current every day. The monthly Fisherman's Post report, published Aug. 3 and now 20 days old, has whiting and black drum in the surf on shrimp and sand fleas, tarpon to 110 pounds and a 63-pound cobia off the Jolly Roger's king rigs, and specks, pompano and Spanish to 3 pounds at Surf City pier. Flounder stays catch-and-release until the Sept. 1 opener.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier station runs over an hour ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No water temperature runs today - NOAA returned none, and the Wrightsville Beach station is the only one this pipeline may quote.
